sanskrit: teṣāṃ na tāvan nirvṛttaṃ vartate tu trayodaśam ajñātavāsaṃ bībhatsur athāsmābhiḥ samāgataḥ
english: Their term of exile has not yet expired — the thirteenth year of incognito dwelling is still in progress — and yet Arjuna (Bībhatsu) has now come and engaged us in battle.

sanskrit: anivṛtte tu nirvāse yadi bībhatsur āgataḥ punar dvādaśa varṣāṇi vane vatsyanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: If Bībhatsu has come before the term of exile has ended, the Pāṇḍavas will have to dwell in the forest for twelve more years.

sanskrit: lobhād vā te na jānīyur asmān vā moha āviśat hīnātiriktam eteṣāṃ bhīṣmo veditum arhati
english: Either through greed they have miscalculated, or delusion has overtaken them; whether their reckoning falls short or exceeds the term, Bhīṣma is best able to determine this.

sanskrit: arthānāṃ tu punar dvaidhe nityaṃ bhavati saṃśayaḥ anyathā cintito hy arthaḥ punar bhavati cānyathā
english: When matters are disputed there is always doubt, for an affair considered one way turns out another way altogether.

sanskrit: uttaraṃ mārgamāṇānāṃ matsyasenāṃ yuyutsatām yadi bībhatsur āyātas teṣāṃ kaḥ syāt parāṅmukhaḥ
english: Among those who were pursuing Uttara and eager to fight the Matsya army, if Bībhatsu has come, who among them would turn his back in flight?

sanskrit: trigartānāṃ vayaṃ hetor matsyān yoddhum ihāgatāḥ matsyānāṃ viprakārāṃs te bahūn asmān akīrtayan
english: We came here to fight the Matsyas on behalf of the Trigarta kings; the Matsyas had done many wrongs to them and spoken ill of us.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ bhayābhipannānāṃ tad asmābhiḥ pratiśrutam prathamaṃ tair grahītavyaṃ matsyānāṃ godhanaṃ mahat
english: To them when they came to us in fear we gave our pledge: first they were to seize the vast cattle wealth of the Matsyas.

sanskrit: saptamīm aparāhṇe vai tathā nas taiḥ samāhitam aṣṭamyāṃ punar asmābhir ādityasyodayaṃ prati
english: It was arranged with them that on the seventh day in the afternoon they would act, and on the eighth day we would advance at sunrise.

sanskrit: te vā gāvo na paśyanti yadi va syuḥ parājitāḥ asmān vāpy atisaṃdhāya kuryur matsyena saṃgatam
english: Either they do not see the cattle, or they have been defeated; or they may have been deceived and joined forces with the Matsya king against us.

sanskrit: atha vā tān upāyāto matsyo jānapadaiḥ saha sarvayā senayā sārdham asmān yoddhum upāgataḥ
english: Or perhaps Matsya, accompanied by his countrymen and together with his entire army, has come against us for battle.

sanskrit: teṣām eva mahāvīryaḥ kaś cid eva puraḥsaraḥ asmāñ jetum ihāyāto matsyo vāpi svayaṃ bhavet
english: Among them some mighty champion has come forward to conquer us, or it may be Matsya himself who has come in person.

sanskrit: yady eṣa rājā matsyānāṃ yadi bībhatsur āgataḥ sarvair yoddhavyam asmābhir iti naḥ samayaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: If it is the king of the Matsyas who has come, or if it is Bībhatsu who has come, we must all fight — this is the agreement we made.

sanskrit: atha kasmāt sthitā hy ete ratheṣu rathasattamāḥ bhīṣmo droṇaḥ kṛpaś caiva vikarṇo drauṇir eva ca
english: Then why do these foremost charioteers stand idle in their cars — Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Vikarṇa, and Drauṇi?

sanskrit: saṃbhrāntamanasaḥ sarve kāle hy asmin mahārathāḥ nānyatra yuddhāc chreyo 'sti tathātmā praṇidhīyatām
english: All these great warriors are confused in mind at this moment. There is no better course than battle — let that resolve be fixed in each man's heart.

sanskrit: ācchinne godhane 'smākam api devena vajriṇā yamena vāpi saṃgrāme ko hāstinapuraṃ vrajet
english: Once our cattle wealth has been seized, who — even if opposed by the god wielding the thunderbolt or by Yama himself in battle — would go back to Hāstinapura?

sanskrit: śarair abhipraṇunnānāṃ bhagnānāṃ gahane vane ko hi jīvet padātīnāṃ bhaved aśveṣu saṃśayaḥ ācāryaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā tathā nītir vidhīyatām
english: Of those struck down by arrows and routed into the dense forest, which foot soldier could survive? There would be doubt even for the cavalry. Let the teacher be placed in the rear guard, and let our strategy be arranged accordingly.

sanskrit: jānāti hi mataṃ teṣām atas trāsayatīva naḥ arjunenāsya saṃprītim adhikām upalakṣaye
english: He knows the counsel of the Pāṇḍavas, and so he appears to intimidate us; I observe that his special affection is for Arjuna.

sanskrit: tathā hi dṛṣṭvā bībhatsum upāyāntaṃ praśaṃsati yathā senā na bhajyeta tathā nītir vidhīyatām
english: And indeed, upon seeing Bībhatsu approach he sings his praises. Let strategy be devised so that the army does not break and flee.

sanskrit: adeśikā mahāraṇye grīṣme śatruvaśaṃ gatā yathā na vibhramet senā tathā nītir vidhīyatām
english: Like an army without a guide, lost in a vast forest in summer, fallen into the enemy's power — let strategy be devised so that the army does not go astray.

sanskrit: aśvānāṃ heṣitaṃ śrutvā kā praśaṃsā bhavet pare sthāne vāpi vrajanto vā sadā heṣanti vājinaḥ
english: What praise should there be merely upon hearing the neighing of horses from the enemy? Horses neigh at all times, whether standing still or moving.

sanskrit: sadā ca vāyavo vānti nityaṃ varṣati vāsavaḥ stanayitnoś ca nirghoṣaḥ śrūyate bahuśas tathā
english: The winds always blow, Indra always sends rain, and the roar of thunder is heard repeatedly — these are no omens.

sanskrit: kim atra kāryaṃ pārthasya kathaṃ vā sa praśasyate anyatra kāmād dveṣād vā roṣād vāsmāsu kevalāt
english: What business does Arjuna have here, and why is he being praised? It can only be out of desire, or hatred, or sheer anger toward us.

sanskrit: ācāryā vai kāruṇikāḥ prājñāś cāpāyadarśinaḥ naite mahābhaye prāpte saṃpraṣṭavyāḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Teachers are compassionate and wise, and they foresee danger; in this great peril that has come upon us, they should on no account be consulted.

sanskrit: prāsādeṣu vicitreṣu goṣṭhīṣv āvasatheṣu ca kathā vicitrāḥ kurvāṇāḥ paṇḍitās tatra śobhanāḥ
english: In splendid palaces, in learned assemblies, and in pleasant lodgings, those who hold diverse learned conversations — scholars shine there.

sanskrit: bahūny āścaryarūpāṇi kurvanto janasaṃsadi iṣvastre cārusaṃdhāne paṇḍitās tatra śobhanāḥ
english: Performing many wondrous feats before gatherings of people, and in the graceful drawing of the bow — scholars shine in those arenas.

sanskrit: pareṣāṃ vivarajñāne manuṣyācariteṣu ca annasaṃskāradoṣeṣu paṇḍitās tatra śobhanāḥ
english: In discerning the gaps in others' arguments, in understanding human conduct, and in detecting faults in the preparation of food — scholars shine in those matters.

sanskrit: paṇḍitān pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā pareṣāṃ guṇavādinaḥ vidhīyatāṃ tathā nītir yathā vadhyeta vai paraḥ
english: Placing the scholars in the rear, and taking those who praise the enemy's virtues out of the equation, let strategy be arranged such that the foe may be slain.

sanskrit: gāvaś caiva pratiṣṭhantāṃ senāṃ vyūhantu māciram ārakṣāś ca vidhīyantāṃ yatra yotsyāmahe parān
english: Let the cattle be secured and held; let the army form its battle array without delay; and let guards be posted where we shall fight the enemy.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca sarvān āyuṣmato bhītān saṃtrastān iva lakṣaye ayuddhamanasaś caiva sarvāṃś caivānavasthitān
english: Karṇa said: I see that all of the men of this long-lived one are frightened and terrified; they are all disinclined to fight and altogether unsettled.

sanskrit: yady eṣa rājā matsyānāṃ yadi bībhatsur āgataḥ aham āvārayiṣyāmi veleva makarālayam
english: Whether it is the king of the Matsyas who has come or Bībhatsu who has come, I shall hold them back as the shore holds back the shark-filled ocean.

sanskrit: mama cāpapramuktānāṃ śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām nāvṛttir gacchatām asti sarpāṇām iva sarpatām
english: The arrows I release from my bow, with their joints bent, will not turn back once loosed, just as serpents do not turn back when they glide forward.

sanskrit: rukmapuṅkhāḥ sutīkṣṇāgrā muktā hastavatā mayā chādayantu śarāḥ pārthaṃ śalabhā iva pādapam
english: Let the arrows released by my skilled hand — gold-feathered and with very sharp tips — cover Arjuna as locusts cover a tree.

sanskrit: śarāṇāṃ puṅkhasaktānāṃ maurvyābhihatayā dṛḍham śrūyatāṃ talayoḥ śabdo bheryor āhatayor iva
english: Let the sound of the palms striking the bowstring as it drives the fletched arrows hard resound like two kettledrums being beaten.

sanskrit: samāhito hi bībhatsur varṣāṇy aṣṭau ca pañca ca jātasnehaś ca yuddhasya mayi saṃprahariṣyati
english: Bībhatsu, fully composed and trained for thirteen years, has also developed a fondness for battle — he will strike at me with relish.

sanskrit: pātrībhūtaś ca kaunteyo brāhmaṇo guṇavān iva śaraughān pratigṛhṇātu mayā muktān sahasraśaḥ
english: Let the son of Kuntī, being a worthy vessel just as a virtuous brahmin is, receive the torrents of arrows loosed by me in their thousands.

sanskrit: eṣa caiva maheṣvāsas triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ ahaṃ cāpi kuruśreṣṭhā arjunān nāvaraḥ kva cit
english: This great archer is renowned in all three worlds; yet I too, O best of the Kurus, am in no way inferior to Arjuna.

sanskrit: itaś cetaś ca nirmuktaiḥ kāñcanair gārdhravājitaiḥ dṛśyatām adya vai vyoma khadyotair iva saṃvṛtam
english: Let the sky today be seen covered on all sides by golden arrows fletched with vulture feathers, as though filled with fireflies.

sanskrit: adyāham ṛṇam akṣayyaṃ purā vācā pratiśrutam dhārtarāṣṭrasya dāsyāmi nihatya samare 'rjunam
english: Today I shall discharge the undying debt I promised in words long ago to the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, by slaying Arjuna in battle.

sanskrit: antarā chidyamānānāṃ puṅkhānāṃ vyatiśīryatām śalabhānām ivākāśe pracāraḥ saṃpradṛśyatām
english: Let the severed nocks of arrows, shattered between them, be seen drifting about in the sky like locusts.

sanskrit: indrāśanisamasparśaṃ mahendrasamatejasam ardayiṣyāmy ahaṃ pārtham ulkābhir iva kuñjaram
english: I shall afflict Arjuna — whose touch is like Indra's thunderbolt and whose blazing energy equals that of great Indra — as one drives an elephant with firebrands.

sanskrit: tam agnim iva durdharṣam asiśaktiśarendhanam pāṇḍavāgnim ahaṃ dīptaṃ pradahantam ivāhitān
english: That blazing Pāṇḍava fire — hard to assail, fueled by sword, spear, and arrow, burning brightly and scorching enemies — I shall extinguish.

sanskrit: aśvavegapurovāto rathaughastanayitnumān śaradhāro mahāmeghaḥ śamayiṣyāmi pāṇḍavam
english: I, a great cloud with the speed of horses for its forewind, the mass of chariots for its thunder, and showers of arrows for its rain, shall quench the Pāṇḍava fire.

sanskrit: matkārmukavinirmuktāḥ pārtham āśīviṣopamāḥ śarāḥ samabhisarpantu valmīkam iva pannagāḥ
english: Let the arrows released from my bow, like venomous serpents, glide toward Arjuna as serpents converge on an anthill.

sanskrit: jāmadagnyān mayā hy astraṃ yat prāptam ṛṣisattamāt tad upāśritya vīryaṃ ca yudhyeyam api vāsavam
english: Relying on the weapon-lore I received from Rāma Jāmadagnya, that best of sages, and on my own valour, I could fight even Indra himself.

sanskrit: dhvajāgre vānaras tiṣṭhan bhallena nihato mayā adyaiva patatāṃ bhūmau vinadan bhairavān ravān
english: The monkey perched at the top of his banner, struck down by my broad-headed arrow, shall fall to the earth this very day, shrieking terrible cries.

sanskrit: śatror mayābhipannānāṃ bhūtānāṃ dhvajavāsinām diśaḥ pratiṣṭhamānānām astu śabdo divaṃ gataḥ
english: The wail of the spirit-beings dwelling in the enemy's banner, scattered in all directions as I assail them, shall rise up to heaven.

sanskrit: adya duryodhanasyāhaṃ śalyaṃ hṛdi cirasthitam samūlam uddhariṣyāmi bībhatsuṃ pātayan rathāt
english: Today I shall uproot from its very root the thorn that has long been lodged in Duryodhana's heart, by casting Bībhatsu down from his chariot.

sanskrit: hatāśvaṃ virathaṃ pārthaṃ pauruṣe paryavasthitam niḥśvasantaṃ yathā nāgam adya paśyantu kauravāḥ
english: Let the Kauravas today behold Arjuna, his horses slain, his chariot wrecked, desperate in his manhood, heaving breath like a great serpent.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ gacchantu kuravo dhanam ādāya kevalam ratheṣu vāpi tiṣṭhanto yuddhaṃ paśyantu māmakam
english: Let the Kauravas go freely and take whatever wealth they wish, or let them stand in their chariots and watch my battle unfold.

sanskrit: kṛpa uvāca sadaiva tava rādheya yuddhe krūratarā matiḥ nārthānāṃ prakṛtiṃ vettha nānubandham avekṣase
english: Kṛpa said: O son of Rādhā, your mind is always crueller than needful in battle. You do not understand the nature of affairs, nor do you consider their consequences.

sanskrit: nayā hi bahavaḥ santi śāstrāṇy āśritya cintitāḥ teṣāṃ yuddhaṃ tu pāpiṣṭhaṃ vedayanti purāvidaḥ
english: There are many paths of statecraft, deliberated upon by reliance on the scriptures; among them, those who know antiquity declare battle to be the most wicked.

sanskrit: deśakālena saṃyuktaṃ yuddhaṃ vijayadaṃ bhavet hīnakālaṃ tad eveha phalavan na bhavaty uta deśe kāle ca vikrāntaṃ kalyāṇāya vidhīyate
english: Battle suited to the right place and the right time grants victory; that very same battle, if untimely, does not bear fruit here. Valour exercised in the right place and the right time is ordained for prosperity.

sanskrit: ānukūlyena kāryāṇām antaraṃ saṃvidhīyatām bhāraṃ hi rathakārasya na vyavasyanti paṇḍitāḥ
english: An interval should be arranged in harmony with the flow of affairs; the wise do not undertake the burden of the chariot-maker — that is, they do not take on what exceeds their capacity.

sanskrit: paricintya tu pārthena saṃnipāto na naḥ kṣamaḥ ekaḥ kurūn abhyarakṣad ekaś cāgnim atarpayat
english: After careful thought, a direct clash with Arjuna is not advisable for us: alone he defended the Kurus, alone he satisfied the fire god.

sanskrit: ekaś ca pañca varṣāṇi brahmacaryam adhārayat ekaḥ subhadrām āropya dvairathe kṛṣṇam āhvayat asminn eva vane kṛṣṇo hṛtāṃ kṛṣṇām avājayat
english: Alone he maintained brahmacharya for five years; alone he abducted Subhadrā and challenged Kṛṣṇa to single combat from his chariot; and in this very forest he rescued Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) who had been carried away.

sanskrit: ekaś ca pañca varṣāṇi śakrād astrāṇy aśikṣata ekaḥ sāṃyaminīṃ jitvā kurūṇām akarod yaśaḥ
english: Alone he learned the divine weapons from Indra for five years; and alone, having conquered the army of Yama (the disciplined host), he brought glory to the Kurus.

sanskrit: eko gandharvarājānaṃ citrasenam ariṃdamaḥ vijigye tarasā saṃkhye senāṃ cāsya sudurjayām
english: Alone, that subduer of foes, he swiftly defeated in battle the Gandharva king Citrasena and his well-nigh unconquerable army.

sanskrit: tathā nivātakavacāḥ kālakhañjāś ca dānavāḥ daivatair apy avadhyās te ekena yudhi pātitāḥ
english: Likewise the Nivātakavacas and the Kālakhañja demons — invincible even by the gods — were felled in battle by him alone.

sanskrit: ekena hi tvayā karṇa kiṃ nāmeha kṛtaṃ purā ekaikena yathā teṣāṃ bhūmipālā vaśīkṛtāḥ
english: O Karṇa, what exactly have you accomplished here alone in the past, comparable to how those kings were each individually brought under subjection by him?

sanskrit: indro 'pi hi na pārthena saṃyuge yoddhum arhati yas tenāśaṃsate yoddhuṃ kartavyaṃ tasya bheṣajam
english: Even Indra himself is not fit to fight Arjuna in battle; whoever boasts that he will fight him — medicine is what that person needs.

sanskrit: āśīviṣasya kruddhasya pāṇim udyamya dakṣiṇam avimṛśya pradeśinyā daṃṣṭrām ādātum icchasi
english: You desire, without reflection, to pluck the fang of an enraged venomous serpent with your index finger while its right hood is raised.

sanskrit: atha vā kuñjaraṃ mattam eka eva caran vane anaṅkuśaṃ samāruhya nagaraṃ gantum icchasi
english: Or else you wish, wandering alone in the forest, to mount a maddened elephant without a goad and ride it into the city.

sanskrit: samiddhaṃ pāvakaṃ vāpi ghṛtamedovasāhutam ghṛtāktaś cīravāsās tvaṃ madhyenottartum icchasi
english: Or you wish, anointed with ghee and wearing bark garments, to wade through a blazing fire fed with ghee, marrow, and fat.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ yaḥ samudbadhya kaṇṭhe baddhvā mahāśilām samudraṃ pratared dorbhyāṃ tatra kiṃ nāma pauruṣam
english: What kind of manliness is it for someone to bind himself hand and foot, tie a great boulder around his neck, and then try to swim across the ocean with his arms?

sanskrit: akṛtāstraḥ kṛtāstraṃ vai balavantaṃ sudurbalaḥ tādṛśaṃ karṇa yaḥ pārthaṃ yoddhum icchet sa durmatiḥ
english: O Karṇa, whoever — unskilled in arms, very weak — wishes to fight Arjuna, who is skilled in arms and mighty: such a man is one of feeble wit.

sanskrit: asmābhir eṣa nikṛto varṣāṇīha trayodaśa siṃhaḥ pāśavinirmukto na naḥ śeṣaṃ kariṣyati
english: We have kept this lion pinned down for thirteen years; now that the lion is freed from its noose, it will leave none of us alive.

sanskrit: ekānte pārtham āsīnaṃ kūpe 'gnim iva saṃvṛtam ajñānād abhyavaskandya prāptāḥ smo bhayam uttamam
english: We rashly assailed Arjuna sitting apart — like fire concealed in a well — and out of ignorance we have come to face the greatest terror.

sanskrit: saha yudhyāmahe pārtham āgataṃ yuddhadurmadam sainyās tiṣṭhantu saṃnaddhā vyūḍhānīkāḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: Let us fight Arjuna together as he comes, drunk with battle-fury; let the soldiers stand armed and arrayed in formation, ready to strike.

sanskrit: droṇo duryodhano bhīṣmo bhavān drauṇis tathā vayam sarve yudhyāmahe pārthaṃ karṇa mā sāhasaṃ kṛthāḥ
english: Droṇa, Duryodhana, Bhīṣma, you yourself, Drauṇi, and the rest of us — we shall all fight Arjuna together. O Karṇa, do not act rashly alone.

sanskrit: vayaṃ vyavasitaṃ pārthaṃ vajrapāṇim ivodyatam ṣaḍrathāḥ pratiyudhyema tiṣṭhema yadi saṃhatāḥ
english: We six charioteers shall be able to face and fight the resolute Arjuna, raised like Vajra-wielding Indra — if we stand united.

sanskrit: vyūḍhānīkāni sainyāni yattāḥ paramadhanvinaḥ yudhyāmahe 'rjunaṃ saṃkhye dānavā vāsavaṃ yathā
english: Let the troops be arranged in battle formations; as supreme archers, alert and ready, we shall fight Arjuna in battle as the demons once fought Indra.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmovāca na ca tāvaj jitā gāvo na ca sīmāntaraṃ gatāḥ na hāstinapuraṃ prāptās tvaṃ ca karṇa vikatthase
english: Aśvatthāman said: The cattle have not yet been won, nor has the border been crossed, nor has Hāstinapura been reached — and yet you boast, O Karṇa.

sanskrit: saṃgrāmān subahūñ jitvā labdhvā ca vipulaṃ dhanam vijitya ca parāṃ bhūmiṃ nāhuḥ kiṃ cana pauruṣam
english: Men who have won very many battles, gained great wealth, and conquered enemy territory — they do not boast of their manliness at all.

sanskrit: pacaty agnir avākyas tu tūṣṇīṃ bhāti divākaraḥ tūṣṇīṃ dhārayate lokān vasudhā sacarācarān
english: Fire burns without speaking; the sun shines in silence; the earth bears all the worlds with their moving and unmoving beings in silence.

sanskrit: cāturvarṇyasya karmāṇi vihitāni manīṣibhiḥ dhanaṃ yair adhigantavyaṃ yac ca kurvan na duṣyati
english: The duties of the four social orders have been prescribed by the wise — duties by which wealth is to be acquired, and which, when performed, do not taint the doer.

sanskrit: adhītya brāhmaṇo vedān yājayeta yajeta ca kṣatriyo dhanur āśritya yajetaiva na yājayet vaiśyo 'dhigamya dravyāṇi brahmakarmāṇi kārayet
english: A brahmin, having studied the Vedas, should officiate at sacrifices for others and sacrifice for himself. A kṣatriya, relying on the bow, should sacrifice but not officiate for others. A vaiśya, having acquired goods, should arrange for the sacred rites of the brahmin class.

sanskrit: vartamānā yathāśāstraṃ prāpya cāpi mahīm imām sat kurvanti mahābhāgā gurūn suviguṇān api
english: Those of great fortune who live according to the scriptures and have attained their place in this world — the noble ones honour their teachers, even those teachers who may be flawed.

sanskrit: prāpya dyūtena ko rājyaṃ kṣatriyas toṣṭum arhati tathā nṛśaṃsarūpeṇa yathānyaḥ prākṛto janaḥ
english: What kṣatriya who has won a kingdom by gambling deserves to feel satisfied by it — satisfied in such a cruel manner as a common, base person would?

sanskrit: tathāvāpteṣu vitteṣu ko vikatthed vicakṣaṇaḥ nikṛtyā vañcanāyogaiś caran vaitaṃsiko yathā
english: And when wealth is obtained in such a way, what discerning man would boast of it — obtained by fraud and deception, like a trapper who lives by snaring?

sanskrit: katamad dvairathaṃ yuddhaṃ yatrājaiṣīr dhanaṃjayam nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca dhanaṃ yeṣāṃ tvayā hṛtam
english: In which chariot duel did you conquer Dhanañjaya, or Nakula and Sahadeva, whose wealth you claim to have seized?
